reference.method: Static inspection of the matched executable, public symbols, field layouts and virtual slots. No executable was run. This file contains metadata and bounded conclusions, not code bytes or disassembly.

facts.contract: SharedTypes::CreativeItemCategory is All=0, Construction=1, Nature=2, Equipment=3, Items=4, ItemCommandOnly=5, Undefined=6, NumCategories=7. Registry initialization creates category objects for keys 1 through 5. This numeric registry order is not the top-tab display order. Category objects have a name and child-group indexes; the per-group item icon is a separate CreativeGroupInfo member.

facts.contract: The CreativeContent handler delegates to registry initialization. That path clears the previous entries, groups and categories, creates categories, traverses packet groups in array order, then traverses packet entries in array order. It does not alphabetically sort these arrays. Child-group lookup can reuse an existing named group, so this traversal does not establish that duplicate named packet groups always produce distinct UI groups.

facts.contract: Groups are resolved against the created categories 1 through 5. A group with an unsupported category, including All=0 or Undefined=6, is skipped in this path. An empty group name takes addAnonymousGroup; a nonempty name takes addChildGroup. This does not define malformed-input group-index repair or UI visibility of the stored command-only category.

facts.topic: Retained entries and group member order
facts.contract: Entry records are appended with their packet entry index before group assignment. UINT32_MAX or an out-of-range group index leaves the record retained without group membership. An unresolved item also prevents the later group assignment. For a valid item and group, the group records the entry index in encounter order, avoiding a duplicate of the same entry index. Retention alone does not prove search visibility.

facts.topic: Expando input validity and header eligibility
facts.contract: Expando refresh skips invalid, null or zero-count input items. A group header is produced only for a group with at least two recorded members and a valid nonempty icon whose item identifier is nonzero. A single-member group or one without such an icon is represented as ordinary items through this path. Empty groups have no item visit from which to construct a header. These are model-consumer conditions; they do not prove how a malformed wire descriptor is normalized before reaching this model.

facts.contract: ContainerExpandStatus is Normal=0, Expanded=1, Contracted=2, Child=3. A newly constructed qualifying header defaults to Contracted. When refresh is allowed to retain expansion state, it first remembers previous Expanded headers and can restore a matching icon/count header to Expanded. This is not a proof of persistent state across sessions or a complete duplicate-icon policy.

facts.topic: Collapsed child filtering and flat model sequence
facts.contract: _generateCurrentItems copies the flat expando sequence into the current view. After copying a Contracted header it skips following Child entries until the next nonchild. The recovered model functions do not insert blank cells or row-padding records at group boundaries. Pixel wrapping and grid geometry belong to the UI layer and were not inferred from this flat sequence.

limits: These conclusions are for the matched 1.26.51.1/protocol2193 executable only. The separately researched official UI assets are described in creative_ui_assets_findings.json and have their own version boundary.

Native controller behavior for All/search, command-only category5, ungrouped or invalid-group entries, search text matching, and empty-category tab visibility was not recovered. Keeping all entries in a flat search catalog or showing/hiding empty tabs is not established here as exact native behavior.

Duplicate creative entry-ID collision policy, duplicate named-group remapping, malformed packet category/index combinations, zero-count wire-descriptor normalization and unknown-item decoding were not fully recovered.
Matching a header by icon and count can affect expansion retention; full native persistence and identity rules are not reconstructed.
No complete creative inventory or anti-cheat compatibility guarantee follows from these bounded registry/model contracts.
